name: steady
title: Steady state of an ODE system

origin.description: Dispatches to stode, stodes, or runsteady and marks the result as a steady object.
origin.usage: steady(y, time = NULL, func, parms = NULL, method = "stode", ...)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial state. Names are kept when y is a dict.

arguments.name: func
arguments.text: func(time, state, parms) returns a list whose first element is the derivatives.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Passed through to func. NULL when the model has no parameters.

origin.details: A missing time is 0 for the Newton methods and c(0, Inf) for runsteady.
origin.value: A steady list. nspec is the length of y.
origin.example:
fun <- function(t, y, p) list(c(-0.1 * y[1] + 0.02 * y[2], 0.1 * y[1] - 0.2 * y[2]))
steady(y = c(1, 2), func = fun)

translation.description: Dispatches to stode, stodes, or runsteady and marks the result as a steady object.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial state. Names are kept when y is a dict.

arguments.name: func
arguments.text: func(time, state, parms) returns a list whose first element is the derivatives.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Passed through to func. NULL when the model has no parameters.

translation.details: A missing time is 0 for the Newton methods and c(0, Inf) for runsteady.
translation.value: A steady list. nspec is the length of y.
translation.example:
from rootSolve import steady

def fun(t, y, p):
    return [[-0.1 * y[0] + 0.02 * y[1], 0.1 * y[0] - 0.2 * y[1]]]

print(steady([1.0, 2.0], func=fun))
